description: Terms Log Horizon uses when it classifies, scores and recommends. Shown by the Dictionary menu in the TUI. Keep the wording aligned with the README 'Under the hood' section; the Pester suite checks that recommendation types, assessments, tiers, coverage sources, plans, statuses and transform operations match the code.

sections.name: Classification
sections.description: How a table is graded before any cost or coverage is considered.

terms.definition: Security-value data you build detections on: sign-in logs, security alerts, threat intel, audit trails, vulnerability findings, firewall hits, EDR telemetry.
Supporting telemetry: performance metrics, infrastructure diagnostics, network flow volumes, inventory snapshots, configuration baselines, health checks.
Not in the classification database and no heuristic matched (no security token in the name, no rules, no Microsoft prefix, not a generic *Logs name, not high volume).
Classification source: direct lookup in Data/log-classifications.json (481 entries), including custom overrides supplied with -CustomClassificationPath.

Classification source: name tokens (Alert, Incident, Threat, Signin, Logon, Audit, Risk, Detection = primary; Flow, Metric, Diagnostic, Perf, Heartbeat, Health, Inventory, Usage = secondary), then analytics rules present, Microsoft first-party prefix, generic *Logs name, high volume with no detections.

Classification source: a _SPLT_CL table is the Data Lake copy of a parent table created by a Sentinel split transform; it inherits the parent connector and retention recommendation and is classified secondary.
analytics (hot tier) or datalake (Auxiliary / Data Lake candidate) from the database entry.
Minimum recommended total retention for the table: 90, 180 or 365 days, drawn from regulatory and industry guidance (CISA M-21-31, NIST SP 800-92, NCSC-UK, ASD ACSC, NSA).

sections.name: Cost tier
sections.description: Monthly ingestion volume bands. Cost uses billing GB (1000 MB) and the price of the plan observed in the Usage table.

terms.definition: Usage.IsBillable is false for every row (or, when Usage carries no flag, the database marks the table free). Cost is 0.
Less than 1 GB per month.
1 to 10 GB per month.
10 to 50 GB per month.
50 GB per month or more.

sections.name: Detection tier
sections.description: Effective coverage: enabled analytics rules + hunting queries + enabled Defender custom detections + implicit consumers that reference the table.

terms.definition: Nothing references the table.
1 or 2 references.
3 to 9 references.
10 or more references.

sections.name: Assessment
sections.description: Combined verdict from classification, cost tier and detection tier.

terms.definition: Primary with Medium or High detection tier.
Primary with Low detection tier and Low or Medium cost.
Primary with no detections. Write analytics rules to get value from the data.
Primary with Low detection tier and High or Very High cost. Review filtering or splitting.
Secondary with no detections and High or Very High cost. Add rules, filter, or move to Data Lake.
Secondary with little or no detection use at Low or Medium cost.
Ingested at no charge; cost analysis does not apply.
Consumed by Sentinel itself (SecurityIncident, SentinelHealth, Watchlist, Usage ...). Never flagged as missing coverage.

sections.name: Coverage source
sections.description: Where a table's coverage signal comes from (first match wins for display).

terms.definition: An enabled analytics rule or hunting query references the table by name in KQL.
An enabled Defender XDR custom detection references the table.

A rule kind with no KQL consumes the table: Threat Intelligence matching (ThreatIntelIndicators, ThreatIntelObjects), Fusion (SecurityAlert, Anomalies), UEBA (BehaviorAnalytics, UserPeerAnalytics, IdentityInfo), Microsoft incident creation (SecurityAlert). Mapped in Data/implicit-consumers.json.
A platform table Sentinel writes for itself; no rule coverage is expected.
No coverage signal.

sections.name: Recommendation types
sections.description: Sorted High > Medium > Low, then by estimated savings. Savings are current cost minus the same volume at the target rate, never a percentage guess.

terms.definition: Secondary + High/Very High cost + None/Low detections. Move to the Auxiliary / Data Lake plan when the table supports it; falls back to a Basic plan suggestion when only Basic is supported; nothing when neither.
High/Very High cost with zero detections. Add rules, filter, or move to Data Lake.
Streamed from Defender XDR, no Sentinel rules, but XDR custom detections exist. Stop streaming and use the unified XDR portal.
Primary, paid, not a platform table, zero detections. Write analytics rules.
Primary, 20 GB/mo or more, 1 to 3 detections. Apply an ingest-time transformation to cut volume.
Primary, 10 GB/mo or more, at least one detection, no existing transform. Split so detection-relevant rows stay on Analytics and the rest goes to Data Lake.
Usage rows show more than one plan in the period, or the configured plan differs from what Usage observed. Confirm the transition was expected.

A table marked deprecated or legacy in the database is still ingesting. Migrate detections to the replacement tables, then retire the old connector. Informational: no savings are claimed because the ingestion moves rather than disappears.
Workspace default or a table's total retention is below the 90-day baseline. Increase retention.
Paid, non-platform table meets 90 days but sits below its category recommendation (180 or 365). Consider longer total retention.
Analytics table whose interactive (hot) retention is under the 90 days Sentinel includes. Raise it unless the short hot window is deliberate.
A finding from the XDR Checker (see XDR states): a known XDR table not streamed, streamed without coverage, not forwarded to Data Lake, or below the one-year advisory.
A rule scored 70 or higher with at least 5 incidents. Tune or disable the noisy rule.

sections.name: Detection Analyzer
sections.description: Per-rule noisiness scoring from incidents and automation rules (-IncludeDetectionAnalyzer).

terms.definition: Incidents linked to the rule by analytic rule id, then rule name, then a title match.

Incidents closed by automation divided by total incidents. Primary source: SentinelHealth automation rule runs by enabled close-incident or playbook rules. Fallback: automation rule conditions (analytic rule id, title and severity, ANDed like Sentinel does). Rules whose conditions are only status, tactics or entities are treated as applying to every incident.
Incidents classified FalsePositive divided by total incidents.
(Volume percentile x 0.35) + (AutoClose percentile x 0.40) + (FalsePositive percentile x 0.25), each percentile ranked across rules that have incidents.
Score 70 or higher. The rule likely needs tuning or disabling.
Score 50 to 69. Early signs of noisiness.
Score below 50.
ScoreStatus: the rule has incidents and at least 3 rules have incidents, so percentiles carry meaning.
ScoreStatus: the rule has incidents but fewer than 3 rules do, so there is nothing to rank against. Score shows N/A.
ScoreStatus: no incidents correlate to the rule. Listed only.

sections.name: Table plans
sections.description: Log Analytics table plans as reported by the Tables API and priced from Usage.Plan.

terms.definition: Full-featured hot tier. Default price 5.59 USD/GB (-PricePerGB). Interactive retention is included for 90 days.

Reduced-cost plan for troubleshooting data. Default 1.15 USD/GB (-BasicPricePerGB). Interactive retention fixed at 30 days. Only tables in Data/basic-plan-tables.json and DCR-based custom tables support it.

Data Lake plan for high-volume verbose logs. Default 0.20 USD/GB (-LakePricePerGB, ingestion + processing). Only tables in Data/auxiliary-plan-tables.json and DCR-based custom tables support it; Classic custom tables do not. Plan switching to or from Auxiliary is not supported by the Tables API.
Whether the table can live on the Auxiliary plan, from the feature matrix and the custom-table rules above.
The table inherits its interactive retention from the workspace default rather than an explicit value.
The table has no explicit long-term retention; total equals interactive.

sections.name: Lifecycle status
sections.description: Optional status on a database entry, shown as a badge in the TUI and reports.

terms.definition: The connector is retired or ingestion has stopped (for example ThreatIntelligenceIndicator after 2025-07-31, Azure Functions connectors replaced by codeless connectors).
An older collection path with a documented successor (for example Log Analytics agent tables such as DnsEvents, or V1 connectors with a V2 table).
The table names to migrate detections to. Present whenever a status is set; may be empty when nothing replaces the table.
Defender tables only. true for the 21 tables the Defender XDR connector streams; false for portal-only and Vulnerability Management tables, which the XDR Checker never treats as streaming candidates.
true for tables Sentinel consumes itself; they receive the Platform assessment and are never flagged as missing coverage.

sections.name: XDR states
sections.description: Defender XDR connector streaming state per known XDR table, and the XDR Checker finding types.

terms.definition: Known XDR table with no workspace copy. Data is only in XDR Advanced Hunting with 30-day retention.
XDRState of a streamed XDR table: the plan of its workspace copy.
Streamed from XDR but no Sentinel rule or Defender custom detection references it.
Streamed on Analytics with no archive or Data Lake retention configured.
Streamed XDR table whose total retention is under the one-year advisory for XDR telemetry.

sections.name: Transform types
sections.description: Operations found in a DCR transformKql, in order of first appearance; multi-operation transforms are joined with '+', anything unrecognised is Custom.

terms.definition: | where: drops rows before ingestion.
| project-away: removes named columns.
| project: keeps only the listed columns.
| extend: adds computed columns.
| summarize: aggregates rows.
No recognised operation; inspect the KQL.
A Sentinel condition-only filter (the portal prepends 'source | where') that routes matching rows to Analytics and the rest to a _SPLT_CL Data Lake copy.
